definition: Deliberation means long and careful consideration or discussion before reaching a decision.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word deliberation. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know deliberation should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Only after months of deliberation did the scholarship committee narrow two hundred applications down to a single winner.
A passing thought weighs a choice for only a moment, while deliberation examines it from every side.
Reflection is quiet thinking about something, but deliberation is a focused, sustained weighing of options before a decision.

Contemplation is quiet, often solitary deep thought — you can contemplate a painting or the stars with no decision anywhere in view. Deliberation is aimed: careful weighing, often through discussion, in order to decide something. Contemplation may wander wherever it likes; deliberation works toward a verdict.

Consideration is a general weighing of factors — lighter and quicker, as in 'after some consideration.' Deliberation is longer, more careful, and often collective: the way a jury or committee talks a decision through. A moment's thought is consideration; days of weighing and debate are deliberation.

Forethought is planning done ahead of time, before a situation even arrives — packing a spare tire shows forethought. Deliberation happens once the decision is actually in front of you: sustained weighing of real options. Forethought looks ahead to what might come; deliberation digs into the choice at hand.

After two full days of deliberation, during which the jurors re-read the transcripts and argued over every piece of testimony, the jury finally returned its verdict.
Two full days of re-reading transcripts and arguing over testimony before deciding is exactly the long, careful weighing of a decision that deliberation describes.
The related adjective 'deliberate' (done on purpose) and verb 'deliberate' (to weigh options) share the root but shift meaning; deliberation always names the careful weighing process itself.
The plural 'deliberations' often refers to a jury's or committee's closed-door discussions.

When the old river bridge was condemned, the town of Marlow had two replacement designs and one chance to choose well.
The council could have voted that first week; instead it scheduled six public hearings, one for every neighborhood the bridge would serve.
Engineers answered questions until midnight; ferry captains, cyclists, and shop owners each got the floor; every cost estimate was read aloud twice.
The deliberation ran from April to September, and people grumbled about the pace — until the vote came, and even the losing side agreed it had been heard.
The steel arch opened two years later, and no one in Marlow calls those five months wasted anymore.
